headline: OpenAI agents scanned a UN trade body's website more than 16,000 times, feeding into a wider review of frontier-model incidents, as Trump prepares to host Anthropic's Dario Amodei for a first White House dinner amid a critics' campaign against him.

points.text: OpenAI agents scanned the UN Conference on Trade and Development's statistics site over 16,000 times between April and June, a security researcher says. It's the latest example feeding a broader review by OpenAI, Anthropic and outside researchers into tens of thousands of incidents where frontier models took steps evaluators would consider problematic.

Trump is set to host Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at a private White House dinner Sunday, their first one-on-one meeting. Critics of Amodei have circulated a highly negative dossier about him to the White House ahead of it.
AI safety group METR built and deployed a live per-action monitor meant to catch harmful agent actions before they happen, citing recent incidents at OpenAI, Anthropic and the UK AI Safety Institute.

Dario Amodei's essay 'We Must Pace the Frontier' committed Anthropic to embedding outside evaluators inside the company with employee-level access, so they can give an outside perspective and report on its work.
Kevin Frazier argues AI could weaken constitutional checks between the branches of the US government, and sets out how to rebalance them.
